back: International trade without government restrictions such as tariffs and quotas.
Policies that restrict imports to protect domestic firms and jobs.
A tax on imported goods; ad valorem (percentage of value) or specific (per unit).
A limit on the quantity or value of a good that may be imported.
Tariff: any quantity at a higher price, earns revenue. Quota: fixed quantity, no tax revenue.
Tariffs, quotas, embargoes, exchange control, licences and red tape, subsidies, product standards.
Infant industries, jobs, anti-dumping, balance of payments, revenue, strategic industries, health and safety, retaliation.

front: Who gains and who loses from a tariff
back: Gain: domestic competitors, government revenue. Lose: firms using imported inputs, importers, consumers, exporters facing retaliation.
Selling goods abroad below their cost of production to capture a market.
